To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the amount of water that can be removed in the first drying pass is directly related to harvest MC and the drying air conditions.

1) the maximum amount of MC that can be removed in a single drying pass is directly related to the harvest MC of the rice, and 2) the tempering duration required for the rice kernels to return to the original MC profile is directly related to this maximum MC removal.

the amount of tempering time necessary to prevent fissuring is dependent on the amount of moisture removed from the grain during the initial drying pass and that a temperature above Tg during the initial drying is not required to achieve high head rice yields.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms that lead to fissure development in rough rice during the drying process and how these mechanisms can be manipulated to improve rice milling quality.
the development and evaluation of new drying and processing technologies for the rice industry.
determining the maximum amount of MC that can be removed during a single drying pass, and the associated temper durations required to prevent fissure formation and quality reductions
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the amount of MC that can be removed from a rice kernel in the initial drying step is directly related to the MC of the kernel and the drying temperature and relative humidity (RH) of the air.
the amount of MC that can be removed from a kernel during an initial drying pass was inversely proportional to the HMC of the sample.
the amount of MC that could be removed during the initial drying pass is a function of the initial HMC and the air drying condition used.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found a strong relationship between the amount of moisture removed in the first drying pass and the amount of tempering required to prevent fissure formation during cooling.
the Tg of the rice kernel plays an integral part in the drying process.

the amount of tempering required to prevent HMY reductions increased with the MC of rice removed in the initial pass and that the amount of MC that can be removed from rice kernels in a single pass is inversely related to the initial MC of the rice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amount of MC removal per drying pass is directly related to the tempering duration.
rice quality is reduced when the rice is dried at temperatures above the Tg of the rice kernel.
the amount of tempering required to prevent Hry reductions is directly related to the amount of MC removal during the drying pass.
